strategy: Use the five unchanged prerequisite modules, especially Reduction.lean, to compose two componentwise perturbations. Define exactProductTree by mapping each pair (a,b) to a*b, roundedProductTree by mapping it to model.mul a b, and roundedDotProduct as roundedSum model of roundedProductTree. First establish IsPerturbation model.u from exactProductTree to roundedProductTree using the relative-error multiplication specification. Apply roundedSum_exists_perturbation to roundedProductTree at its unchanged depth d to obtain an existential perturbed tree P whose exactSum is roundedDotProduct. Compose these relations with IsPerturbation.trans. The resulting bound u + gamma d u * (1 + u) equals gamma d u + u * (1 + gamma d u), which gamma_step bounds by gamma (d+1) u. Use IsPerturbation.mono to obtain the original target. Thus the witness is the perturbed rounded-product tree supplied by the addition theorem, now proved to be a perturbation of the exact-product tree. This is a construction plan, not a completed target proof.

Do not alter prerequisites or configuration; use only local Lean, Mathlib, and approved sources. The planner itself must not edit /workspace.

Define exactProductTree (tree : Tree (ℝ × ℝ)) : Tree ℝ as tree.map (fun p => p.1 * p.2). Define roundedProductTree (model : Model) tree as tree.map (fun p => model.mul p.1 p.2). Define roundedDotProduct model tree as roundedSum model (roundedProductTree model tree). These definitions must actually implement multiplication rounding followed by addition rounding.

Record that both product maps preserve the original tree shape and depth, using Tree.depth_map. In particular, the addition theorem on roundedProductTree has depth exactly tree.depth, including for a single leaf and unbalanced trees.

Establish for every model and pair tree that IsPerturbation model.u (exactProductTree tree) (roundedProductTree model tree). Induct on tree; at a leaf use model.round_spec (a*b) and Model.mul to derive |model.mul a b - a*b| = |a*b| * |δ| ≤ model.u * |a*b|. Combine child relations with IsPerturbation.node. This must handle zero and signed products without division by a product.
Set d = tree.depth. From (((d+1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * model.u < 1) and model.u_nonneg derive (d : ℝ) * model.u < 1. Manage natural-to-real casts explicitly. Obtain 0 ≤ gamma d model.u using gamma_nonneg.

Apply roundedSum_exists_perturbation model (roundedProductTree model tree), rewriting depth via Tree.depth_map and using the derived smallness hypothesis. Retain the returned witness P, its relation IsPerturbation (gamma d model.u) (roundedProductTree model tree) P, and P.exactSum = roundedDotProduct model tree. The witness must be constructed by the supplied theorem, not assumed.

Use IsPerturbation.trans with first bound model.u and second bound gamma d model.u, justified by gamma_nonneg. Obtain IsPerturbation (model.u + gamma d model.u * (1 + model.u)) (exactProductTree tree) P. This relation accounts for the multiplication rounding and all additions on each leaf path.

Rewrite the composed scalar bound by commutative-ring algebra as gamma d model.u + model.u * (1 + gamma d model.u). Apply gamma_step d model.u model.u_nonneg with the original (d+1)-smallness assumption, then IsPerturbation.mono, to reach exactly gamma (d+1) model.u. No gamma monotonicity lemma or stronger smallness assumption is required.

State a final theorem universally over model : Model and tree : Tree (ℝ × ℝ), assuming only (((tree.depth + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * model.u < 1), concluding ∃ P : Tree ℝ, IsPerturbation (gamma (tree.depth + 1) model.u) (exactProductTree tree) P ∧ P.exactSum = roundedDotProduct model tree. The IsPerturbation relation expresses equal shape and the leafwise bound |perturbedProduct - a*b| ≤ gamma (tree.depth+1) model.u * |a*b|. Preserve the existential componentwise backward-error claim, rather than substituting a scalar forward-error estimate or an exact-arithmetic restriction.
